item.title: Official Python SDK Released for the Scrapfly Platform
item.description:
Official Python SDK Released for the Scrapfly Platform

The official Python SDK for the Scrapfly platform has been released, providing tools for web scraping, screenshots, AI extraction, crawling, and a remote anti-bot browser.

🧩 Overview

  • Integrates with Scrapy, LlamaIndex, and LangChain.
  • Covers Scrapfly API endpoints including web scraping, screenshots, AI extraction, crawling, and a remote anti-bot browser.
  • Features optional installation extras for added capabilities and performance.

⚙️ Key details

  • AsyncScrapflyClient added in 1.0.0 provides every method of ScrapeClient as coroutines, with streamed methods (scrape_batch, crawl_prompt) as async iterators.
  • Up to 0.12, ScrapflyClient runs a call as a coroutine with async_scrape, async_screenshot, and async_extraction, while concurrent_scrape is an async generator.
  • The unblocker parameter (previously named asp) turns on anti-bot bypass for blocking solutions such as Cloudflare, DataDome, PerimeterX, or Akamai.

🚀 Availability

Extra Purpose
speedups Brotli compression and msgpack serialization
parser Built-in HTML parser (lxml, beautifulsoup4, extruct)
scrapy Scrapy integration
browser Playwright-based cloud browser helpers
browser-use Browser-use agent integration
webhook-server Native webhook server using flask
concurrency Kept for compatibility; concurrency needs no extra dependency
  • The speedups and webhook-server extras install brotli (CPython) or brotlicffi.
  • Up to 0.12 they installed the archived brotlipy, requiring users to run pip uninstall brotlipy before upgrading.

#Python #WebScraping #Scrapfly #Automation #SDK

item.title: Rust SDK Adds Stable 2026-07-28 MCP Version with New Features
item.description:
Rust SDK Adds Stable 2026-07-28 MCP Version with New Features

This release brings the stable MCP 2026‑07‑28 specification to the Rust SDK, while remaining fully compatible with the 2025‑11‑25 release and earlier versions.

🔍 Overview

  • The SDK implements the stable MCP 2026-07-28 specification.
  • It remains fully compatible with the 2025-11-25 release and previous versions.

🧩 Features

  • Server discovery & negotiation
  • Transport‑neutral subscriptions
  • Long‑running tasks
  • Response caching
  • Multi‑round‑trip requests
  • Standard HTTP routing headers

⚙️ SDK Structure

  • Repository crates:
    • rmcp: core crate providing the RMCP protocol implementation
    • rmcp‑macros: procedural macro crate for generating RMCP tool implementations
  • Basic dependencies:
    • tokio
    • serde
  • JSON Schema generation (version 2020‑12):
    • schemars

📦 Installation & Setup

  • Add the latest published version: 
    1

    cargo add rmcp --features server
  • Or use the dev channel: 
    1

    cargo add rmcp --features server --git https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk --branch main

🚀 Server and Client Lifecycle

  • serve() uses the legacy MCP lifecycle:
    • The client sends initialize.
    • The server returns negotiated server information.
    • The client sends notifications/initialized.
  • Use ClientServiceExt::serve_with_lifecycle to select another lifecycle explicitly.
  • ClientLifecycleMode::Initialize is equivalent to the existing serve() behavior.
  • Discover startup does not send notifications/initialized; discovery completes startup.
  • Each subsequent request carries its protocol version, client information, and capabilities in _meta.
  • For a server, serve() waits for peer input that establishes the protocol lifecycle, such as initialize from a legacy client.
  • A stdio MCP server is normally launched by an MCP client as a child process.
  • Running the executable alone in a terminal can leave this await pending because no client has sent protocol messages yet.
  • After serve() returns, the service handles messages in the background.
  • You can run other asynchronous work, then use waiting() to wait for shutdown.
  • To cancel during startup, use serve_with_ct().

🛠️ Building a Service

  • Use ServerHandler or ClientHandler to build a service.
  • Await protocol startup, then receive a handle to the running service.

#Rust #MCP #SDK #Async #JSON

Source: modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk

item.title: Stagehand released as an SDK for building and interacting with browser agents
item.description:
Stagehand released as an SDK for building and interacting with browser agents

Stagehand is an SDK released for building and interacting with browser agents. It allows developers to extract data and interact with any site on the web.

🧩 How it works

Stagehand is designed to manage browser sessions efficiently by handling persistence and security:

  • Session Persistence: Cookies persist in ./browser-data, so the next run starts already signed in.
  • Security: The observe() method returns real selectors, ensuring that credentials never reach the model.
  • Integration: Users can get started with Claude Code, Codex, Eve, Mastra, and more.

⚙️ Key details

The SDK provides specific methods for interacting with web interfaces, with each function serving a distinct purpose:

Method Function
act() Self-heals when the site redesigns its form.
extract() Returns schema-validated data.
observe() Returns real selectors so credentials never reach the model.

💡 Why it matters

The tool enables developers to sign in once, keep the session, and pull structured data out the other side. This workflow supports reliable automation by maintaining state between runs and validating the data returned by the agent.

#Stagehand #BrowserAgents #SDK #WebAutomation #ClaudeCode

Source: browserbase/stagehand

item.title: Milvus Java SDK Splits Into Two Packages From v2.5.2
item.description:
Milvus Java SDK Splits Into Two Packages From v2.5.2

The Milvus Java SDK has been restructured starting with version 2.5.2. The SDK is now split into two separate packages: milvus-sdk-java and milvus-sdk-java-bulkwriter. This change was made because BulkWriter requires a significant number of dependencies.

🧩 Available Packages

  • milvus-sdk-java: The core Milvus Java SDK package
  • milvus-sdk-java-bulkwriter: A separate package for BulkWriter functionality

⚙️ Key Details

The Milvus Java SDK has the following requirements:

  • Java 8 or higher
  • Build tools: Apache Maven or Gradle
  • SLF4J is required for logging purposes and must be added to the classpath

Developers can add the Milvus SDK to their projects using either:

  • Apache Maven
  • Gradle

🚀 Availability

For Spring Boot applications (Java 17+), the milvus-sdk-java-spring-boot-starter package automatically configures a MilvusClientV2 from milvus.* properties.

Examples for the Java SDK are available in the examples folder.

💡 Contributing

Contributors should:

  • Read the contribution guidelines first
  • Refer to the DEVELOPMENT.md file for development information

item.title: Strands Agents Releases Open-Source SDK for Production AI Agents
item.description:
Strands Agents Releases Open-Source SDK for Production AI Agents

Strands Agents has released an open-source SDK for building and running production AI agents in Python and TypeScript. The SDK allows developers to build an agent harness and control it end-to-end across any model and any cloud.

🔍 Overview

Strands Agents provides a model-driven approach to building AI agents in a few lines of code. It is designed for developers who would otherwise write their own agent loop, as it runs within the user’s process with no hosted control plane.

⚙️ Key Details

The SDK includes a variety of built-in capabilities for agent management and observability:

  • Lifecycle Controls: Token budgets, turn limits, stop reasons, and cancellation.
  • Agent Capabilities: Structured output, tools, and MCP.
  • Architecture Patterns: Memory, sessions, and multi-agent patterns.
  • Operations: Streaming, guardrails, tracing, and evals.
  • Model Portability: Ability to swap backends when scaling while keeping code the same.

🧩 How it works

The project is maintained as a monorepo containing the following components:

Component Description Access/Platform
Python Strands harness Fully assembled agent via create_harness() PyPI
TypeScript Strands harness Fully assembled agent via createHarness() npm
strands CLI Prototype and chat with a harness agent from the terminal npm
Python SDK Agent loop, model providers, and tools PyPI
TypeScript SDK Agent loop, model providers, and tools npm

💡 Why it matters

The SDK is model agnostic, providing first-class support for Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Amazon Bedrock, as well as custom providers. It provides context management, execution limits, and observability built in before any configuration is written, and the agent loop traces every decision.

#OpenSource #AIAgents #Python #TypeScript #SDK

Source: strands-agents/harness-sdk

item.title: Introduction of Pydantic AI and Pydantic AI Harness
item.description:
Introduction of Pydantic AI and Pydantic AI Harness

Pydantic AI has been released as a Python AI SDK providing a typed, extensible agent loop where models can be changed via a string swap.

🔍 Overview

The SDK allows the same agent to run across various environments, including:

  • Web frontends
  • Terminals
  • Voice calls
  • Durable background queues
  • GitHub Actions
  • As a plain object called via run()

🧩 How it works

Component Function
Pydantic AI Python AI SDK for typed data extraction and agent loops
Pydantic AI Harness Provides capabilities for complex, long-running work including memory, guardrails, planning, and storage
Pydantic Graph Separate package for typed control flow
Pydantic Evals Separate package for testing agent behavior similar to pytest
Pydantic Logfire AI observability platform for the entire app
Pydantic AI Gateway Model key management with real-time cost monitoring and budget control
genai-prices Maintains current model pricing
Monty Sandboxed Python interpreter for running model-written code

⚙️ Key details

  • Capabilities: Pydantic AI includes image generation and embeddings. Pydantic AI Harness can be used to build a complete coding agent featuring workspace-rooted file access, an allowlisted shell, repo orientation, and context management for long sessions.
  • Integration: The Gateway supports self-hosting and uses plain OpenTelemetry instrumentation, ensuring compatibility with existing backends.
  • Scope: The system supports a range of use cases from simple typed data extraction to complex multi-agent collaboration.

#PydanticAI #Python #AIAgents #LLM #SDK

Source: pydantic/pydantic-ai

item.title: Asqav Releases Python and TypeScript SDKs for AI Agent Evidence
item.description:
Asqav Releases Python and TypeScript SDKs for AI Agent Evidence

Asqav has released Python and TypeScript SDKs to provide verifiable evidence of AI agent actions through an evidence layer.

🔍 Overview

The SDKs enable AI agents to generate signed, hash-chained compliance receipts for every action. These receipts are timestamped against independent witnesses and can be verified by auditors, regulators, or counterparties without an Asqav account.

🧩 How it works

  • Cryptography: Server-side cryptography is used, meaning there are zero native dependencies in either SDK.
  • Algorithms: The algorithm used is per-receipt from signature.alg, utilizing ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204, post-quantum) for cloud-issued receipts and Ed25519/ES256 for locally signed ones.
  • Verification:
    • Users with a signature_id can verify without an API key.
    • The verify() function returns a public verdict and recomputes the chain_hash locally as the SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical payload.
    • Offline, zero-trust checks that reproduce the signature can be performed via asqav.verify_receipt_offline(receipt, jwks) in Python, verifyReceiptOffline() in TypeScript, or a standalone CLI command: python -m asqav.verifier.verify_receipt --offline.

⚙️ Key details

Component Details
Python SDK pip install asqav (Requires Python 3.10+); tested on 3.10, 3.11, 3.12
TypeScript SDK npm install @asqav/sdk (Requires Node 20.19-20.x or 22.12+); tested on Node 20, 22
Integrations Works with LangChain, CrewAI, and MCP
Diagnostics asqav doctor validates configuration and connectivity when ASQAV_API_KEY is set

🚀 Availability

Asqav offers three plans:

  • Free: No credit card required.
  • Pro: Paid monthly or annual subscription.
  • Enterprise: Custom and volume-priced.

This development is profiled in the IETF Internet-Draft draft-marques-asqav-compliance-receipts and the Independent Submission profiling draft-farley-acta-signed-receipts.

#AIagents #SDK #Cryptography #Compliance #PostQuantum

Source: jagmarques/asqav-sdk
